blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reliable evaluation of visual 3D reconstruction and depth estimation in vegetation-rich outdoor environments is limited by the scarcity of geometric ground-truth data and the cost of complete scanner surveys. We present a LiDARbased reference-generation pipeline for evaluating the zero-shot performance of feed-forward visual-geometry models alongside conventional structure-from-motion (SfM) methods. The pipeline reuses camera images, LiDAR scans, and reference poses from existing multi-sensor localization datasets to generate per-view depth maps and visible reference point clouds. To address visibility errors in accumulated LiDAR scans, we introduce the LargeDepth-Gap Visibility Score (LDGVS) for point-wise visibility filtering and automatic scale selection in Hidden Point Removal(HPR). Experiments on TartanAirV2 and TartanGround show that, compared with Poisson surface reconstruction, which is an approach suited to completed scan surveys, the combined HPR and LDGVS filtering retains approximately three times the point density at comparable absolute relative error. We also apply the pipeline to the BotanicGarden dataset to systematically compare depth estimation and 3D reconstruction methods. Feedforward methods produce dense depth predictions efficiently, but their 3D reconstructions can contain duplicated structures. Conventional SfM generally produces more coherent geometry, but its reconstructions remain sparse and more prone to failure in challenging vegetated scenes. The benchmark toolkit and datasets will be released.
blocks.zh: 对植被丰富的室外环境中的视觉立体重建和深度估计的可靠评价受到以下因素的限制:几何地面真实数据稀缺,扫描仪调查费用也很高。 我们提出一个基于LiDAR的参考生成管道,用于评价向导的视觉几何模型的零射性能,以及常规的结构自动方法。 管道再利用相机图像,LiDAR扫描,以及来自现有多传感器本地化数据集的参考面,生成每个视图深度图和可见参考点云. 为了解决累积的LiDAR扫描中的可见度错误,我们在隐藏点清除(HPR)中引入了用于点向可见度过滤和自动比例选择的大型深度-Gap可见度分数(LDGVS). 对TartanAirV2和TartanGround的实验显示,与Poisson表面重建(一种适合完成扫描调查的方法)相比,HPR和LDGVS综合过滤在可比绝对相对误差时保留了大约三倍的点密度. 我们还将管道应用于BotanicGarden数据集,以系统比较深度估计和立体重建方法。 FeedForward方法能高效地产生密集的深度预测,但其3D重建可以包含重复的结构. 常规SfM一般能产生更连贯的几何特征,但其重建仍然稀少,在挑战性的植被场景中更容易失败. 将发布基准工具包和数据集。

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Visual depth estimation and 3D reconstruction are essential capabilities for agricultural and other field robots, providing dense geometric information from lightweight, low-cost cameras. Many studies [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] have sought to improve visual geometric methods in vegetation-rich outdoor environments, including forests, orchards, crop fields, and botanical gardens.
However, agricultural applications continue to rely predominantly on conventional geometry-based SLAM [ 5 , 6 ] or SfM [ 7 , 8 ] , while the feed-forward methods [ 8 , 9 , 10 ] have been less widely adopted. This pattern contrasts with general-purpose 3D-reconstruction and depth-estimation benchmarks [ 11 , 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 ] , where feed-forward models are increasingly prominent [ 16 , 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 ] .
This motivates us to evaluate their zero-shot performance in vegetation-rich outdoor environments.
blocks.zh:
视觉深度估计和3D重建是农业和其他野外机器人的基本能力,从轻量级低成本相机提供密集的几何信息. 许多研究[1,2,3,4]都试图改进植被丰富的室外环境中的可视几何方法,包括森林,果园,农作物田地和植物园.
然而,农业应用仍然主要依赖以传统几何学为基础的SLAM[5,6]或SfM[7,8],而饲料向导方法[8,9,10]则不太被广泛采用. 这种模式与通用的3D-重建与深度估计基准[11,12,13,14,15]形成对比,其中向导模型越来越突出[16,17,18,19,20,21,22].
这促使我们评价他们在植被丰富的室外环境中的零射出性能.

blocks.en:
However, benchmarking in these environments remains challenging because publicly available datasets with suitable ground-truth (GT) geometry are scarce and acquiring such data is time-consuming and labor-intensive. A standard approach is to use high-accuracy terrestrial laser scanners to capture complete and dense scans of the environment [ 14 , 15 ] . This process, however, requires professional surveying expertise and substantial manual effort for data acquisition, scan registration, and outlier removal. These requirements make complete surveys particularly costly in extensive and structurally complex vegetation-rich outdoor environments. A few studies have used laser scanners [ 8 , 23 , 24 ] to
obtain GT geometry in such environments, but the resulting datasets are often limited in scale and not fully publicly available.
blocks.zh:
然而,在这些环境中制定基准仍然具有挑战性,因为具有适当地真相几何特征的公开数据集很少,获取这类数据既费时又费力。 一种标准方法是使用高精度地面激光扫描仪来捕捉环境的完整而密集的扫描. [14, 15]. 然而,这一进程需要专业的调查专门知识和大量人工数据采集、扫描登记和删除外部数据。 这些要求使得在广泛和结构复杂的植被丰富的户外环境中进行完整的调查特别昂贵。 一些研究使用了激光扫描仪[8、23、24]至
在这种环境中获得GT几何,但所产生的数据集在尺度上往往有限,不完全公开.

blocks.en: To address this gap, we investigate repurposing mobile LiDAR measurements from existing multi-sensor localization datasets as geometric references. Mobile LiDAR enables data collection over large areas, and a growing number of datasets provide camera images, LiDAR scans, and reference trajectories in agricultural and other vegetation-rich outdoor environments, as summarized in Table I . Although these datasets contain large-scale observations of complex scenes, they were developed primarily for localization and mapping rather than for benchmarking visual depth estimation or 3D reconstruction. Consequently, they do not directly provide camera-aligned reference depth or visibility-filtered 3D geometry. Previous studies have demonstrated the use of LiDAR-derived references for depth estimation and 3D reconstruction in urban and road environments [ 25 , 11 , 26 , 27 , 28 , 29 ] , but extending this approach to vegetation-rich environments remains challenging. The difficulty arises because mobile LiDAR measurements are sparse and nonuniform and may be affected by motion distortion. Accumulating multiple scans improves point density but can introduce visibility errors caused by incomplete observations, occlusions, and camera–LiDAR parallax.
blocks.zh: 为了弥补这一差距,我们调查从现有的多传感器本地化数据集中重新使用移动LiDAR测量作为几何参考. 如表一所概述,移动的LiDAR使大面积数据收集成为可能,越来越多的数据集提供相机图像、LiDAR扫描以及农业和其他植被丰富的室外环境的参考轨迹。 虽然这些数据集包含对复杂场景的大规模观测,但它们的开发主要是为了本地化和绘图,而不是为视觉深度估计或3D重建设定基准. 因此,它们不直接提供相机相通的参考深度或能见度过滤的3D几何. 以往的研究表明,在城市和道路环境的深度估计和立体重建中使用了LiDAR衍生的参考文献[25、11、26、27、28、29],但将这种方法推广到植被丰富的环境仍然具有挑战性。 出现这种困难的原因是移动的LiDAR测量很少且不统一,可能受运动扭曲的影响. 累积多相扫描可以提高点密度,但可以引入由不完全观测,隐蔽,相机-LiDAR参数所引发的能见度差.

blocks.en:
These limitations raise a central question: how can mobile LiDAR data be converted into reliable camera-view geometric references for benchmarking visual depth estimation and 3D reconstruction in vegetation-rich environments? We therefore develop a reference-generation pipeline and apply it to the representative BotanicGarden [ 30 ] dataset, where the generated references are used to compare feed-forward visual-geometry models with conventional SfM methods.
Our contributions are summarized as follows: 1. We propose a pipeline that converts camera, LiDAR, and reference-pose data from existing localization datasets into per-view depth and visible point-cloud references. 2. We introduce the Large-Depth-Gap Visibility Score (LDGVS) for point-cloud visibility filtering and automatic Hidden Point Removal (HPR) scale selection, providing greater reference density than Poisson surface reconstruction at comparable absolute relative error. 3. With the proposed pipeline, we construct a BotanicGarden benchmark comparing feed-forward visual-geometry models with conventional SfM methods in geometric quality, metric scale, cross-frame consistency, robustness, and efficiency.
blocks.zh:
这些局限性提出了一个中心问题:如何将移动的LiDAR数据转换成可靠的相机-视图几何参考物,用于在植被丰富的环境中对视觉深度估计和三维重建进行基准评估? 因此,我们开发了一个参考生成管道,并将其应用到具有代表性的BotanicGarden[30]数据集中,其中生成的参考用于将饲料前向可视-几何模型与传统的SfM方法进行比较.
我们的贡献概述如下: 1. 我们提议建立一个管道,将相机、LiDAR和现有本地化数据集的参考数据转换成可视深度和可见点云参考数据。 2. 我们采用大深度-Gap能见度分数(LDGVS),用于点-云能见度过滤和自动隐藏点清除(HPR)分量选择,比出相可比的绝对相差误差的波森地表重建提供更大的参考密度. 3. 通过拟议的管道,我们构建了一个BotanicGarden基准,在几何质量、度量尺度、跨框架一致性、稳健性和效率方面,将饲料前向可视-几何模型同传统的SfM方法进行比较。

blocks.en: II-A Agricultural Datasets for 3D Reconstruction and Depth Estimation
blocks.zh: II-A 用于三维重建和深度估算的农业数据集

blocks.en:
Many studies have investigated 3D reconstruction using agricultural data.
Some studies use RGB-D cameras to obtain GT data in apple orchards [ 42 ] ,
a walnut-tree scene [ 43 ] .
some studies evaluate performance through comparisons with SOTA methods [ 10 , 9 ] ,
whereas others rely solely on visualization [ 5 ] .
Several studies evaluate their results using manual measurements [ 6 , 44 ] .
Laser scanners are more commonly used to provide more accurate and denser GT data for
tree reconstruction [ 8 , 23 , 24 ] .
To our knowledge, no work has used LiDAR data as GT for 3D reconstruction or depth estimation in this type of environment.
Several LiDAR-based depth-estimation
benchmarks exist for urban and road environments [ 25 , 11 ] .
And some localization datasets [ 26 , 27 ] has been
used for 3D reconstruction evaluation [ 28 , 29 ] .
Although many studies have explored this topic,
the availability of datasets for large-scale 3D reconstruction and depth estimation
in agricultural environment remains limited.

blocks.en:
To filt this gap, we propose a LiDAR-based geometric reference-generation
pipeline for data collected directly by lightweight mobile robot platforms.
This eliminates the need for dense, exhaustive scanning,
thereby enabling the cost-effective creation of large-scale 3D reconstruction
and depth estimation datasets.
blocks.zh:
为了填补这一空白,我们提议采用基于LiDAR的几何参考生成法。
用于轻量级移动机器人平台直接收集数据的管道。
这就不需要进行密集、详尽的扫描了,

blocks.en: II-B Point-Cloud Visibility Analysis for Dataset Consturction
blocks.zh: II-B 数据集相接的点-可见度分析

blocks.en:
For fair comparison, we only can compare the point cloud that can be seen
in image data. Therefore the key problem of datasets for 3D reconstruction and
depth estimation using point cloud data is to get correct visible the point-cloud. Specifically,
ETH3D and ScanNet++ datasets [ 14 , 45 ] use
Poisson surface reconstruction on laser-scan point
clouds [ 46 ] to render depth rather than
directly using projected point clouds.
More loosely, splatting-based methods [ 47 , 48 ] render a primitive projection.
These approach can work well when dense and complete geometry is available,
but sparse LiDAR scans in vegetation-rich scenes often contain missing areas and
large depth discontinuities.
In such cases, surface reconstruction may fail to represent the scene.
Another approach relies on consistency [ 11 ] or
depth differences [ 49 ] between estimated depth and projected point-cloud depth.
These methods can work well in urban and road environments,
but depth estimates are often inaccurate in vegetation-rich environments.
Consequently, these methods may also filter out too many visible points.
Hidden Point Removal (HPR) [ 50 ] analyzes visibility on the point cloud without first
reconstructing a surface. However, we found that
HPR cannot be applied directly to environments with large depth variations. [ 51 ] proposed visibility score can be computed directly in image space.
However, this work only evaluate their method on two manual label points of city scene, can not
generalize well in our experiments.

Instead, in this work, we propose a modular point-cloud visibility-analysis
framework that introduces a large-depth-gap visible score
and uses it to adaptively select the HPR radius,
enabling robust removal of occluded LiDAR points in sparse,
unevenly sampled scenes with large depth variations.
blocks.zh:
相反,在这项工作中,我们提出模块化的点-云能见度-分析

blocks.en: II-C 3D Reconstruction and Depth Estimation in Vegetation-rich and Agricultural Scenes
blocks.zh: II-C 3D 植被丰富和农业场景的重建和深度估计

blocks.en:
Recent reviews [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] indicates that most research on agricultural applications still based on traditional SfM or SLAM.
For examples, some studies integrate existing vSLAM frameworks with semantic-segmentation networks for semantic 3D reconstruction of orchards [ 5 , 7 , 6 ] .
SfM is the most widely used method for 3D reconstruction in plant phenotyping. [ 52 , 53 ] .
There is also work on applying the improved SFM to agricultural scenarios, such as detector-free [ 8 ] and deep learning matcher [ 54 , 55 ] .
blocks.zh:
最近的审查[1、2、3、4]表明,大多数农业应用研究仍然基于传统的SfM或SLAM。
例如,一些研究将现有的 vSLAM 框架与语义分类网络相融合,用于果园的语义3D重建 [5, 7, 6].
SfM是植物花序中最广泛使用的3D重建方法. [52.53].
还开展了将改进后的可持续森林管理应用于农业情景的工作,例如无探测器[8]和深层学习匹配器[54.55]。

blocks.en:
On the other hand, due to the emergence of visual self-supervised large models [ 56 ] these emerging feed forward methods show a very strong generalization across different
scenes and benchmarks [ 17 , 19 , 57 , 21 , 18 ] .
However, These methods have not yet been fully benchmarked in agricultural scenarios against
traditional SfM methods.
blocks.zh:
另一方面,由于视觉自我监督的大型模型的出现[56],这些新兴的饲料前行方法显示出一种非常强烈的泛指,跨越了不同的.
[17、19、57、21、18]。
不过, 这些方法尚未在农业假想中充分参照
传统的SfM方法.

blocks.en:
Therefore, we construct a comprehensive
3D-reconstruction and depth estimation benchmark to evaluate the performance of SfM and feed forward methods in large-scale vegetation-rich and agricultural environments.
We also integrate recent state-of-the-art learning-based feature and matching models [ 58 , 59 , 60 ] into an SfM pipeline and compare their performance within this benchmark.
blocks.zh:
因此,我们构建了一个全面的
3D-重构和深度估计基准,用于评估SfM在大型植被丰富和农业环境中的性能和饲料前进方法.
我们还将最近最先进的基于学习的特征和匹配模型[58、59、60]纳入SfM管道,并在此基准范围内比较其绩效。

blocks.en:
A direct combination of existing techniques, such as Poisson surface
reconstruction and SGM-based depth-consistency filtering, can produce reliable
projected depths where the reconstructed geometry is accurate. However, these
methods cannot always faithfully reconstruct complex forest and agricultural
environments. Errors and missing structures in the reconstruction can therefore
cause valid projected depth samples to be incorrectly rejected, as demonstrated
by the experimental results in
Section V-A .
To address this problem, we organize occluded-point removal into three
complementary visibility-analysis modules: (i) the Large-Depth-Gap Visible Score,
which evaluates local projected-depth discontinuities; (ii) Automatic Hidden
Point Removal (AHPR), which uses this score to select the HPR scale; and
(iii) Depth-Consistency Visibility Analysis, which checks projected points
against a dense depth estimate.

blocks.en: VI Conclusion
blocks.zh: 六. 结论

blocks.en: We presented a LiDAR-based pipeline that converts camera, LiDAR, and reference-pose data from existing multi-sensor localization datasets into per-view depth maps and visible point-cloud references for benchmarking visual depth estimation and 3D reconstruction in vegetation-rich outdoor environments. To address visibility errors in the accumulated LiDAR measurements and enable their reuse as geometric references, we introduced the Large-Depth-Gap Visibility Score (LDGVS) for point-wise filtering and automatic scale selection in Hidden Point Removal (HPR). The resulting pipeline reduces reliance on dedicated laser-scanner surveys. Experiments on TartanAirV2 and TartanGround show that the combined HPR and LDGVS filtering retains approximately three times the reference density of Poisson surface reconstruction at comparable absolute relative error.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了基于LiDAR的管道,将相机,LiDAR,以及现有多传感器本地化数据集的可引用数据转换成每个视图的深度图和可见点-云的参考数据,用于在植被丰富的室外环境中进行目视深度估计和3D重建的基准. 为了解决所积累的LiDAR测量中的能见度差并使其能够被再用为几何参考,我们引入了"大深度-Gap能见度分数"(LDGVS),用于在"隐藏点清除"(HPR)中进行点向过滤和自动比例选择. 由此产生的管道减少了对专用激光扫描仪的依赖。 关于TartanAirV2和TartanGround的实验显示,HPR和LDGVS综合滤波法在可比绝对相差误差时保留了约3倍于普瓦生地表重建的参考密度.

blocks.en: We instantiated the pipeline on BotanicGarden to compare the zero-shot performance of representative feed-forward visual-geometry models with conventional SfM in an under-evaluated vegetation-rich outdoor setting. Feed-forward models generate dense geometry efficiently but can exhibit duplicated structures and cross-frame inconsistencies, whereas conventional SfM produces more coherent geometry but remains sparse and prone to failure. These findings demonstrate the need for domain-specific evaluation and the value of the benchmark in exposing trade-offs in density, consistency, robustness, and efficiency beyond geometric accuracy alone.
blocks.zh: 我们通过波塔尼克加登的管道进行了即时分析,以将具有代表性的饲料前向视觉几何模型的零发性能与评价不足的富于植被的室外环境中的常规SfM进行比较。 饲料前向模型能高效地产生密集的几何结构,但可以显示重复结构和跨框架不一致,而常规的SfM则产生更连贯的几何结构,但仍很稀少并容易出故障. 这些调查结果表明,需要针对具体领域进行评价,而且基准在暴露密度、一致性、稳健性和效率方面的取舍方面的价值超出精确度的几何范围。

blocks.en: S.VI Qualitative Depth-Error Analysis
blocks.zh: S.VI 定性深度-误差分析

blocks.en:
Figure 11 illustrates the sources of depth error.
Even the aligned left-view single scan in (b) has residual errors at object
boundaries: sparse LiDAR samples and discrete ground-truth pixels can fall on
different surfaces near a depth discontinuity. The right-view cumulation
baseline in (c) also retains incorrect depths within objects because of
camera–LiDAR parallax and accumulated occluded points. PSR in (e) retains
low-error interiors but removes much of the difficult boundary support,
whereas AHPR(5%)+LDGVSF(0.7) in (k) preserves denser support with residual
errors mainly at edges. Since accuracy is evaluated on each method’s retained
pixels, these additional boundary samples help explain the accuracy–coverage
trade-off.
